## Final report (fix landed)

**Problem.** Scheduled Mirror Guard replication check reds the run on a single instantaneous sample of expected, self-healing Gerrit->GitHub replication lag (run 32567576681; next run +16min passed).

**Proven root cause.** The primary watcher (mirror-guard.yml -> `python -m rebar.mirror_guard --replication`) had no evaluation window: run() fetched once and mapped one diverged sample to exit 1, while the module's own design (docstring shipped in d96628c9dca) delegates transient-lag absorption to the alarm layer's sustained-divergence window — implemented only on the CloudWatch secondary (monitoring_ws7.tf 2x5-min). Legitimacy: incomplete-implementation (cited design authority in the RCA comment above). Proof: local credential-free runtime experiments — single diverged sample -> exit 1; converged -> exit 0 — plus static confirmation the workflow has no retry/window.

**Defect origin.** caused_by a774-5ca9-3a80-4f6d (sweaty-seal-braid), by scope-of-work: the omission shipped with a774's own commit d96628c9dca; no later commit broke it (workflow history reviewed: 26d60938d27, 80a4a152beb, d7c5aa0097a, 1384806642f, 7b6e2ad0e31 — all non-semantic). Recorded on the close as --class=plan_defect --caused-by=a774-5ca9-3a80-4f6d.

**Test (RED->GREEN, held out).** 5 new behavioral tests in tests/unit/test_mirror_guard.py: transient-lag-converges (the mechanism test — seen RED on unfixed code: exit 1), persistent-static-tip stays exit 1 with 'stalled' + samples=3, moving-never-converging tip stays exit 1, in-sync first sample costs 1 fetch/0 sleeps, missing SHA fails immediately. Tests were held out of the fix subagent's tree; mutation check (re-seeded single-sample behavior via attempts=1) returned the oracle to RED, restore returned 30/30 GREEN.

**Fix.** src/rebar/mirror_guard.py: in-process evaluation window `_replication_check_with_lag_tolerance` (default 3 samples, 45s apart, ~6x the documented ~15s lag; `_sleep` seam; run() lag_attempts/lag_delay_seconds; CLI --lag-attempts/--lag-delay); healthy on convergence, unhealthy otherwise — strictly no weakening (today's failure set minus lag-that-converges; GitHub-ahead/foreign never converges so it stays exit 1 every run). Portable: lives in the module, works under any scheduler (no CI-provider state). Workflow header comment updated; replication_verdict unchanged (still instantaneous truth).

**Landed.** Gerrit change 2110 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2110), LLM-Review +1 (4 non-blocking advisories, incl. a note that the static-vs-moving reason is trivially 'static' at attempts=1 — cosmetic, defaults use 3) and Verified +1 (CI run 32573665947 SUCCESS); merged to main as 969acad79b4b.

**Scope & safety.** Caller sweep: only callers are the workflow (comment-only change), the credential-boundary suites tests/scripts/test_residual_drain_* (15 passed, 1 skipped), and the guard's own tests — no behavioral dependency on single-sample failure. Restoration-not-creation: completes the cited designed capability (incomplete-implementation carve-out); no new dependency (stdlib time only); no test weakened (test_run_divergence_exit_1 gained a no-op sleep injection, assertion unchanged).

**Siblings.** Axis 1 (construct: single-sample check of eventually-consistent replication state as an alarm): none — the only other replication watcher (observability.sh section 5 -> CloudWatch) publishes instantaneous samples by design and its alarm layer already has the sustained window (monitoring_ws7.tf:40-44); the ruleset check watches persistent (non-self-healing) state, so single-sample is correct there. Axis 2 (parity): rule = 'replication divergence alarms only when persistent'; surfaces: CLI/workflow (fixed), library run() (same core, fixed), CloudWatch probe (window at alarm layer, present), MCP tool (N/A — none exists), dual-direction (N/A — read-only check).

**Residual risk.** A merge burst outlasting the ~90s in-run window would still red the run; window is tunable via --lag-attempts/--lag-delay and the 15-min cron retries — accepted (matches the CloudWatch design's temporal-absorption approach; no ancestry probing added). 3ff9-a8f0 precedent cited as supporting noise-class authority only; the controlling authority was the guard's own design text, so no operator ruling extension was needed.

**Replication.** Original report replayed through the real CLI entry (main(['--replication']) with the incident's SHA sequence): exit 0; a stuck mirror (static GitHub tip): exit 1. Original problem no longer reproduces; true outages stay loud.
